Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Security review session - proposed times

Hi Sarah / Chris —

Thanks again for agreeing to a short security review session. To make sure we have the right folks on the call, I'd like to confirm attendees from both sides and propose a couple of time slots next week. From Redwood we'll have: myself (AE), Ethan Park (SE, will cover architecture/perf and network flows), and Irene Choi (Security; will cover compliance, SOC2, data handling).

Proposed 45-minute slots (PST):
- Tue Feb 17, 10:00–10:45 AM PST
- Tue Feb 17, 2:00–2:45 PM PST
- Wed Feb 18, 9:30–10:15 AM PST

If none of those work, send a couple alternatives and we'll try to accommodate. I'll attach our security pack and the questionnaire we referenced. Also happy to include procurement for any legal/contract questions — looping them on follow-ups as needed.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[dylan.brooks@redwood.ai] [M: (555) 210-3344]

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the options. Our security team is available on Tue Feb 17 but only in the afternoon Eastern (which is 11:00–1:00 PST). The 2:00 PM PST slot would be too late for them. Can we do Tue Feb 17 at 12:00 PM PST (3:00 PM ET)? That would be 12:00–12:45 PM PST.

Also, please confirm that someone from Redwood security (Irene) will be on the call to cover SOC 2 controls, data residency, and encryption-at-rest keys. Procurement (cc'd) has a few contract redlines to flag, but we can keep that to the end of the session or follow up separately. I've attached our security questionnaire; if you could have Irene scan it prior to the meeting that'd be great.

Thanks —
Sarah Connors

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai

Cc: ethan.park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security review session - proposed times

Hi all —

I can make the Tue 2/17 12:00 PM PST slot and will review the Acme questionnaire this morning. Quick notes after a skim:
- SOC 2: we can provide the most recent Type II report and map controls to questionnaire items; I'll attach the redacted report to the invite.
- Encryption/KMS: we use customer-specific keys for private deployments; for hosted API we use KMS with strict key management and rotation — I can pull the KMS architecture diagram for the call.
- Data residency & retention: will prepare our retention matrix and a short summary of options (hosted vs private).

Ethan — can you prepare a short network/dataflow diagram (5–7 slides) showing where tokens and payloads live during inference and how KV caching behaves? That will help answer some of Chris's engineering questions.

Irene Choi
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: chris.tan@acme.com

One request: our engineering manager had a last-minute conflict and asked if we can shift by 30 minutes to 12:30 PM PST (3:30 PM ET). If that works for Redwood attendees, we prefer 12:30–1:15 PM PST so we have full overlap. If not, we can proceed at 12:00.

If 12:30 works, can you update the calendar invite and include the redacted SOC2 and the network diagram slides mentioned?

Appreciate it —
